# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-002 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-101 (sotorasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
In this open-label, single-arm Phase 1/2 study, treatment activity will be assessed against historical response rates without a concurrent control group or blinded independent review.
Results from the expansion cohort will serve as the primary efficacy package for the planned marketing application, and the sponsor will proceed without a formal FDA meeting regarding the cohort design, development plan, or submission requirements.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
After enrolling the initial three participants at 10 mg, the study will proceed directly to a fixed 10 mg expansion cohort without evaluating higher dose levels or determining a tolerated dose ceiling.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
After the recommended Phase 2 dose is selected from tolerability data, all subsequent participants will receive that dose without any randomized comparison of alternative dose levels or formal dose-response analysis.
Dose-response analyses will be limited to the randomized expansion cohort, and data from dose-escalation participants and other nonrandomized cohorts will not be included.
All participants will receive the fixed 200 mg dose supplied in a single capsule strength throughout the study, with no alternative strengths available for dose evaluation.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

tasks.rationale: SMILES가 있으므로 구조 계열(반응성 warhead)을 분류하고 ChEMBL 효력값 분포를 확보한다. 독성 장기는 구조에서 추론하지 않는다.
타겟/계열(KRAS G12C)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 5개·증량 규칙(BOIN)이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
대상국 US의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).
적격기준 또는 방문표가 있으므로 ClinicalTrials.gov에서 유사시험 설계 구조를 비교한다(효능 정답으로 쓰지 않는다).

ev_012.section: 3.2 다양한 용량을 비교하기 위한 임상시험 설계
ev_012.quote:
• 품목 허가시 권장 용량을 뒷받침하기 위해서는 항종양 활성, 안전성 및 내약성을 
평가하는 임상시험에서 다양한 용량을 비교해야 한다.
 - 적절한 경우 추가 평가가 필요한 용량의 선정 시 유사한 계열 또는 동일한 작용 
기전의 약물에 대한 자료도 활용할 수 있다.
- 5 -
 - 모델링 방법은 비교할 용량을 파악하고 선정할 때 참고할 수 있다.
 - 용량 탐색 시험에서 새로운 용량 수준에 대한 코호트를 평가하거나 기존 용량의 
코호트에 더 많은 환자를 모집(backfill cohort)하는 방법은 추가 개발을 고려 
중인 용량에 유용할 수 있다. 이와 같은 방법을 통해 다양한 용량을 비교하는 
임상시험을 시작하기 전에 안전성과 활성을 비교한 추가 자료를 확보할 수 있다.
• 다양한 용량을 비교하기 위한 임상시험에서는 무작위 배정, 평행 설계의 용량 반응 
임상시험을 권장한다.
 - 무작위 배정 방식은 개별 용량을 투여한 환자 간의 비교 가능성을 높이고 
용량-반응 및 노출-반응 관계를 평가할 때 편향을 최소화한다. 비교 가능성을 더 
개선하는 방법으로 층화 무작위 배정 방식을 사용할 수도 있다.
 - 더 높은 용량이 활성을 개선하는 것과 관련이 있다는 편향이 발생할 수 있으므로 
용량군 배정에 대한 환자 및 연구자의 눈가림을 고려할 수 있다.
 - 개별 용량 단계에서는 안전성 및 항종양 활성을 충분히 평가할 수 있는 규모로 
계획해야 한다. 치료적 임상시험의 수준으로 제1종 오류를 사용하여 용량 간의 
통계적 우월성 또는 비열등성을 입증하기 위한 검정력을 고려할 필요는 없다.
 - 활성과 관련된 측정은 종양 평가 기반의 평가변수(예: 전체 반응률, 무진행 생존 
기간) 및 기타 조직, 혈액 또는 영상 기반 평가변수를 포함할 수 있다.
 - 임상시험 중 중간 분석을 통해 활성 및/또는 안전성을 평가하고, 하나 이상의 
용량에 대한 등록을 중단하기 위한 적응적 설계를 고려할 수 있다.
 - 교차를 허용하는 임상시험의 경우는 분석 계획에 교차 투여를 고려한 안전성 및 
활성 평가 방법을 사전에 명시해야 한다.
• 치료적 임상시험의 이전에, 또는 치료적 임상시험의 일부로서 용량군을 추가하는 
방법으로 다양한 용량을 비교할 수도 있다.
 - 다양한 용량과 대조군을 포함하고 하나의 용량이 대조군 대비 우월한 유효성을 
입증하도록 설계한 치료적 임상시험은 제1종 오류를 강력하게 통제해야 한다.

ev_013.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

ev_015.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_015.quote:
The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and 
well-being and the reliability of trial results. The sponsor should adopt a proportionate and risk-
based approach to quality management , which involves incorporating quality into the design 
of the clinical trial (i.e., quality by design) and identifying those factors that are likely to have 
a meaningful impact on participant s’ rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of the 
results (i.e., critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)). The sponsor should describe 
the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH 
E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports). 
ICH E6(R3) Guideline 
28

ev_016.document_title: ICH E6(R3) Good Clinical Practice — Principles and Annex 1
ev_016.quote:
Risk control should be proportionate to the importance of the risk to participant s’ 
rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of trial results. Risk mitigation 
activities may be incorporated, for example, in protocol design and implementation, 
monitoring plans, agreements between parties defining roles and responsibilities, and 
training.  
Where relevant, the sponsor should set pre-specified acceptable ranges (e.g., quality 
tolerance limits at the tr ial level) to support the control of risks 
to critical to quality factors. These pre -specified ranges reflect limits that when 
exceeded have the potential to impact participant safety or the reliability of trial 
results. Where deviation beyond these ranges is detected , an evaluation should be 
performed to determine if there is a possible systemic issue and if action is needed.

Problems with Titration Designs 
A study design widely used to demonstrate  effectiveness utilizes dose titration to 
some effectiveness or safety endpoint.  Such titration designs, without careful 
analysis, are usually not informative about dose-response relationships.  In many 
studies there is a tendency to spontaneous improvement over time that is not easily 
distinguishable from an increased response to higher doses or cumulative drug 
exposure.  This leads to a tendency to choose, as a recommended dose, the highest 
dose used in such studies that was reas onably well-tolerated.  Historically, this 
approach has often led to a dose that was well in excess of what was really necessary, 
resulting in increased undesirable effects, e.g. to high dose diuretics used for 
hypertension.  In some cases, notably where an early answer is essential, the

The purpose of this guidance is to provide advice to sponsors regarding the design and conduct 
of first-in-human (FIH) clinical trials intended to efficiently expedite the clinical development of 
oncology drugs, including biological products, through multiple expansion cohort trial designs.2 
These are trial designs that employ multiple, concurrently accruing subject cohorts, where 
individual cohorts assess different aspects of the safety, pharmacokinetics, and antitumor activity 
of the drug product.  
This guidance provides FDA’s current thinking regarding (1) characteristics of drug products

information to include in investigational new drug applications (INDs) to support the use of 
individual cohorts; (3) when to interact with FDA on planning and conduct of multiple expansion 
cohort trials; and (4) safeguards to protect subjects enrolled in FIH expansion cohort trials.

ev_035.document_title: Expansion Cohorts: Use in First-in-Human Clinical Trials to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics
ev_035.section: A Assessing Safety of Recommended Phase 2 Dose
ev_035.quote:
Expansion cohorts can be intended to further evaluate safety beyond the initial dose-escalation 
portion of a trial. These studies should be supported by detailed information on available safety 
and PK data from the dose-escalation phase and a summary of safety data from other expansion 
cohorts, if available. In situations when there is a narrow therapeutic index and dose-limiting 
toxicities have been observed in the dose escalation phase that may be fatal or result in serious 
morbidity, FDA strongly recommends that expansion be delayed until sufficient data are 
available to determine the recommended phase 2 dose to help ensure subjects safety.

Randomization to several fixed dose groups (the randomized parallel dose-
response study) is simple in concept and is a design that has had extensive use 
and considerable success.  The fixed dose is the final or maintenance dose; 
patients may be placed immediately on that dose or titrated gradually (in a 
scheduled “forced” titration) to it if that seems safer.  In either case, the final dose 
should be maintained for a time adequate to allow the dose-response comparison.

theoretically necessary in all cases; a positive slope, even without a placebo group, 
provides evidence of a drug effect.  To measure the absolute size of the drug effect, 
however, a placebo or comparator with very limited effect on the endpoint of 
interest is usually needed.  Moreover, because a difference between drug groups 
and placebo unequivocally shows effectiveness, inclusion of a placebo group can

T00_protocol_scan.position: The protocol is internally irreconcilable: direct 10 mg expansion precludes the stated 180–960 mg BOIN escalation and selection of two candidates from escalation data. It therefore lacks executable material supporting its own dose-selection rationale or comparison of multiple doses.

T04_exposure_dose_relationship.position: Appendix D is unavailable. The synopsis does not provide exposure metrics, exposure-response methods, populations, covariates, or quantitative selection criteria. This is material because sotorasib has nonlinear, time-dependent PK and unknown exposure-response relationships. The protocol therefore lacks assessable material supporting its integrated RP2D rationale.

T05_design_oc.position: Appendix C is unavailable. A target DLT rate, dose list, maximum sample, and statement that four simulations occurred do not permit assessment of BOIN conduct or operating characteristics. Essential escalation/de-escalation, overdose control, stopping, evaluability, replacement, and scenario-specific simulation results are missing.

T07_regulatory_clause_search_US.position: Sixty randomized subjects are not justified by the supplied material. FDA guidance recommends sizing each dosage arm for sufficient safety and activity assessment and justifying sample size for clinically important differences; registrational superiority power is not necessarily required. Effect assumptions, precision, analysis, multiplicity, and decision-error characteristics are absent.

T06_regulatory_clause_search_KR.position: The MFDS civil guide recommends multidose comparison and prespecified excessive-toxicity stopping criteria; it is nonbinding. The synopsis lacks cohort-specific population composition, sample-size rationale, futility/toxicity stopping rules, and closure criteria, preventing assessment of the randomized expansion.

T03_class_label_check.position: The routine liver-test schedule matches the cited sotorasib label schedule. However, the label calls for more frequent testing after transaminase and/or bilirubin abnormalities; that provision is not stated. No supplied clause establishes a distinct schedule based solely on recent immunotherapy.

T08_analog_trial.position: Evidence is insufficient to determine whether a fixed four-week anti-PD-(L)1 washout adequately mitigates hepatotoxicity. The supplied sotorasib label evidence gives liver-monitoring instructions but does not provide a washout interval or quantify risk by time since immunotherapy.
